title: Share KDE laptop's WiFi to Android smartphone over Bluetooth
line: Bluetooth settings now have a "Share Internet connection" switch that lets paired phones get online through the computer.
explanation: Plasma's Bluetooth settings could only join a phone's Bluetooth network (NAP); there was no way to host one, so users needed blueman-services to share their laptop's connection with a phone. The Bluetooth KCM's Settings page now has a "Share Internet connection" switch. Turning it on adds and activates a NetworkManager bridge connection (pan0) with a Bluetooth NAP setting and IPv4 "shared", so NetworkManager registers the network server with BlueZ and gives connected devices DHCP and NAT; turning it off deletes that connection. Its UUID is kept in bluedevilglobalrc, and the switch follows NetworkManager's active connections.

commits.message:
kcm: add a switch to share the Internet connection over Bluetooth

Plasma could connect to a phone's Bluetooth network, but couldn't offer
its own connection to paired devices. The settings page now has a switch
that adds a NetworkManager bridge acting as a Bluetooth network server.

BUG: 523139

media.caption: Bluetooth settings on master: no way to share the computer's connection
New "Share Internet connection" switch, turned on: the NAP bridge connection is created and active
If NetworkManager refuses, the error is shown and the switch goes back off
